study type: Prospective observational study with cross-sectional measurements
cohort: The study included 400 randomly selected and consenting women who had undergone a Caesarean section at a tertiary facility in Ghana.
finding: Pain management was deemed inadequate within the first 12 hours post-CS, particularly with movement (93% inadequate), and was less adequate for women with one previous surgery or a CS lasting longer than 45 minutes.
cross-section timing: 6-12 hours post-CS (at rest and with movement) and 24-36 hours post-CS (with movement)
